explanation: Same: no definition of Brahmana because the parts of the Veda cannot be limited, any definition too narrow or too wide, mantra part already given, then the list of kinds; only the Caturmasya reference differs (new 'तै० स० ३।७।१।१' vs Vol 1 'Taittiriya Brahmana 1-7-1-1') and Vol 1 adds Kannada paraphrase.

Same nine examples with same classification (hetu, nirvacana, ninda, prasamsa, samsaya, vidhi, parakriya, purakalpa, specific determination); reference numbers differ (new TS 2.5.3.3 for 'tad dadhno dadhitvam' vs Vol 1 2-5-3-4) and new leaves the damaged 'भापानेव' as 'the word', Vol 1 reads 'masan eva mahyam pacanti' (beans); no clash.

Same: the nine marks occur in mantras too, so 'any of hetu etc.' cannot define Brahmana; same five/eight mantra examples (indavo vam usanti hi, udanisur mahir, mogham annam, agnir murdha divah kakut, adhah svid asid, vasantaya kapinjalan, sahasram ayuta dadat); only the damaged reference for 'mogham annam' (new 10.1.7.3, Vol 1 10-117-6) differs.

Same three further definitions refuted (iti-abundance, 'ity aha' sentence, narrative/akhyayika) with the same examples (rajA cid yam bhagam bhaksity aha; yo va raksah sucir asmity aha; Yama-Yami); references differ: Yama-Yami new 'ऋ. १०|२०' (NOTE, broken) vs Vol 1 10-10, 'yo va raksah' new '७१०५११६' vs Vol 1 7-104-16, purakalpa yajnena yajnam new 10.90.16 = Vol 1 p.484 (Vol 1 p.481 has 1-164-50); new's 'ityaddada' text is damaged, Vol 1 gives 'ityadada ityajatha ityapaca'. Sense untouched.

Same: since Veda has only the two parts and mantra was defined, the remainder is Brahmana; Jaimini's two sutras 'tac codakesu mantrakhya' (3-1-32) and 'sese brahmanasabdah'; same explanation of 'in this Veda certain exhortatory sentences are called mantra by those who know tradition'. Differs only in the number of the second sutra: new 'जै० २।१।३२' (NOTE) vs Vol 1 2-1-33 (and Vol 1 p.482 adds 2-1-34 'amnateu').

Same: objection from the brahmayajna list (itihasa, purana, kalpa, gatha, narasamsi) answered by the Brahmin/parivrajaka principle; same examples (devasurah samyattah; idam va agre naiva kincanasit = purana, creation; kalpa in Arunaketuka chayana; gathas 'yamagathabhih parigayati'; narasamsis = ṛcs on human deeds); conclusion same. New cites TA 2.9, TB 2.2.9.1, TA 1.32.2, TS 5.1.8.2 as Vol 1 does (Vol 1 gives 'yugma-gathabhih' in the Sanskrit, 'yamagathabhih' in its English).

Same: Jaimini-nyayamala verse (no definition of rik/saman/yajus because of mixture; no mixture since pada, giti, praslista-patha are marks) and 'ahe budhniya mantram me gopaya yam rsayas traivida viduh...' with traivida = knower of three / their students, construction 'protect the threefold mantra part'; the new verse is damaged (NOTE) but its sense is Vol 1's.

Same: mixture examples (devo vah savitotpunatu is in the Yajurveda yet called 'savitryarca' ṛc; saman sung in Yajurveda 'etat sama gayann aste'; yajus in Samaveda 'aksitam asi, acyutam asi'; ṛcs as basis of saman), then answer by pada/giti/continuous reading, three Jaimini sutras 2-1-35,36,37, threefold Veda, study of all Vedas or one per Yajnavalkya. Differences: Chandogya reference new '३।१०।६' (scan) vs Vol 1 3-17-6; new says 'these three yajus' but its scan quotes only two, Vol 1 names the third (pranasamsitam asi); sense untouched.

Same: with the one-Veda option the 'own' Veda is the one coming down the paternal line ('svadhyayo 'dhyetavyah'); study is nitya not kamya; Purusarthanusasana sutra 'vedasyadhyayanam nityam anadhyayane patat'.

Same: scripture on the fall ('he who abandons the self-recitation has no share in speech/heaven'), the ṛc 'yas tityaja sacividam sakhayam na tasya vacy api bhago 'sti ... na hi praveda sukrtasya panthaam' (RV 10.71.6), sacivid = Veda that protects like a friend, fruit of sacrifices through mere study, 'yam yam kratum adhite' (TA 2.15), brahmayajna fruit reached through study, worldly talk, 'nanudhyayad bahun sabdan' (SB 14.7.2.23). Vol 1 prints the ṛc with a different (misread) first line and cites TA 1-3-3; new follows the scan (RV 10.71.6); sense same.
Same: hearing poetry and drama is in vain for him, and the smriti 'yo 'nadhitya dvijo vedan anyatra kurute sramam, sa jivann eva sudratvam asu gacchati sanvayah' (Manu 2.168).

Same: mutual dependence between knowing the study-injunction and studying; Guru (Prabhakara) school gets the boy engaged by the teacher's teaching, Prakasatman and others by the father's instruction before study (like the evening worship); either way study is for all initiated; 'adrstartha tv adhitir vihitatvat' (sutra 1) as prima facie that study has an unseen purpose, because eating has no injunction.

Same: 'ghrtakulyadyatidesah svargakalpanam va' - transfer of the arthavada on brahmayajna/japa/study (rivers of ghee, by the ratri-sattra principle) or assume heaven by the Visvajit principle; then the doubt why an unseen is assumed when seen fruits (obtaining, sanctification) are possible.

Same: sutra 3 'ayukte samskaraprapti' (neither is a fitting fruit), the jyotistoma-sentences like snake-poison mantras have no authority in own sense, sutra 4 'anyangam nartha-pramanakam', sutra 5 'adhyayanavakyam ananyangam', objection from tavya = object, sutra 6 'saktuvat karana-parinamah'.

Same: 'saktun juhoti' read as 'saktubhir juhoti' since the flour is burnt to ashes; so here 'with the self-recitation'; sutra 7 'drste tu nadrstam', sutra 8 'drstau praptisamskarau', sutra 9 'praptyartha-bodhah' (arises, understood), avaghata-like restriction, sutra 11 samskara established because both the sacrifice-injunctions and the study-injunction are taken up.

Same: sacrifice-injunctions need the self-recitation for knowledge, the study-injunction excludes reading from writing, hence samskara of the self-recitation; objection that samskara is an unseen potency not belonging to the self-recitation but to the study-coloured effort denoted by tavya (new's 'अध्ययनसच्छतत्वं' is damaged, flagged NOTE).

Same: 'tavyah karmany adrstavaci' (tavya denotes the unseen in the object, nearer than the base's sense), objection 'anyangam' answered since the unseen is subsidiary to an independent unseen and does not obstruct knowledge of own sense; sutra 14 'yathaprapta-upapattyartham na saktunyayah' (natural sense fits, no need to force as with the flour).

vol1_location: l.10353-10446 (p.508-510), sutra 15 and 'sa vicaram aksipet', avaghata
explanation: Same: Bhatta and Guru hold determination of meaning is enjoined since an injunction ends in a human end; objection that study alone does not give it, so the injunction draws in inquiry (Mimamsa); universal rule that injunction impels only what it enjoins/helps answered by 'avidheyanupakaryaksepo 'vaghataavrttivat': 'vrihin avahanti' enjoins pounding not repetition, yet repetition is drawn in to husk; objection on study with the auxiliaries begun.

Same: study with auxiliaries may give meaning but inquiry removes conflicts ('sangadhyayanat tadbhave vicaro virodhapanut'); established view 'praptes tu gavadivat pumarthatvad vidhis tadantah' (cows sought for milk, the injunction ends in obtaining the syllables); sutra 6 'phalavad bodhantatve adhyayanakartsnyam' (Brhaspatisava vs Rajasuya); 'krtsnapraptir japartha'. Vol 1 adds a Kannada note that only kshatriyas perform Rajasuya, no clash.

Same: 'lokavan naijo bodhyah' (understanding is its own, like worldly speech), reply that an eight-year-old initiated boy is an easily found person qualified is set aside, 'so 'kamyah prag bodhyabhanabhanayoh' (known already from father etc. like evening worship, or unknown and so not desirable), objection of general vs particular knowledge, 'uddesayogat' (Agnihotra etc. endless, general aim gives only general fruit).
Same: if there is no aim of understanding, how does the Veda have purport in its own sense; answer 'tatparyam sabdat' (purport established by the word's own power).

Same: the world's utterance with an aim and the objection that without the study injunction ending in understanding Mimamsa would have no impeller, answered by 'vicara uttaravidhiyukta upapadyate'. Differs in wording: new 'uddisya uccaranam dosaghnam loke' = 'uttering with an aim removes faults (produced through connection with a person)', Vol 1 English 'repetition ... will remove one's sins in this world' (but its Kannada comment p.516-517 speaks of doubts like 'composed by men' vanishing, which agrees with new); sense not clashing.

Same: sacrifice-injunctions know the sacrifice only superficially and impel inquiry (Purva-Mimamsa) for removal of conflict, the hearing injunction directly enjoins Brahma-inquiry, while on the view that the study injunction impels it the sacrifice injunction would be useless.

Same: study injunction is binding only on the three classes; for kratu-vicara this is accepted ('ato nityah kratuvicaras traivarnikamatrasya', penalty heard for not doing), for Brahma-vicara refused: 'brahmavicarah punah paramahamsasyaiva'; 'nitya' carried on.

Same: knowledge of meaning is enjoined by another sentence 'brahmanena niskarano dharmah sadango vedo 'dhyeyo jneyas ca' (word 'niskarana' excludes kamya), and Yaska's two sayings (Nirukta 1.18): 'sthanur ayam bharaharah kilabhud adhitya vedam na vijanati yo 'artham', 'yo 'rthajna it sakalam bhadram asnute', 'yad grhitam avijnatam nigadenaiva sabdyate'.

Same: four halves, first praises knowledge, three blame ignorance; Taittiriya ṛc 'ye arvan uta va purane vedam vidvamsam abhito vadanti adityam eva te parivadanti sarve; agnim dvitiyam trtiyam ca hamsam'; 'yavatir vai devatas ta sarva vedavidi brahmane vasanti ... dive dive namaskuryat'. Wording differs: new 'anagnav iva suskaidho' = dry fuel 'on a place without fire', Vol 1 'dry fuel thrown upon ashes'; new 'nasilam kirtayet' = 'should not speak what is improper', Vol 1 'never publicize their faults'; sense compatible, new closer to the Sanskrit.

Same: vedavid = knower of the sense, two kinds (modern teacher skilled in fourteen vidyasthanas, ancient like Vyasa), revilers proud of learning/wealth/birth revile Aditya, then Agni, then Hamsa = Vayu ('hanti' always moving), Veda-knower reaches union with Agni, Vayu, Aditya, all deities dwell in him, daily homage without proclaiming faults; 'sthanu' = branchless dry stump fit only for fuel, mere reciter is not an outcast but gets no fruit; 'kila' marks worldly renown/honour.

Same: vedic text taken from the teacher without sense never blazes, so not Veda in the chief sense; etymology 'vetti by this a means beyond perception and inference' ('pratyaksenanumityā vā yas tūpāyo na budhyate, etam vindanti vedena tasmad vedasya vedata'); Yaska (Nirukta 1.19) cites 'uta tvah pasyan na dadarsa vacam'.

Same: the third pada, Yaska's purport of the first half (the man who sees/hears Speech without knowing: no grammar, e.g. 'vayum eva ... gamayati' / 'adityan eva ... gamayanti'; has grammar but no Mimamsa, e.g. 'yavato 'svan pratigrhniyat' where grammar gives the acceptor, Mimamsa the giver). Differs only in references: the 'vayum eva/adityan eva' text new 'तै. सं. ३।१।१।१' vs Vol 1 note TS 2-1-1-1; Vol 1 adds Purva-Mimamsa 3-4-30.

Same: third pada 'uto tvasmai tanvam visasre' explained with 'svam' = word-sense via grammar and 'jnanam' = purport via Mimamsa, 'uto' = 'api'/'but' distinguishing from the two ignorant men; fourth pada simile 'jayeva patye usati suvasah' = well-clad (auspicious raiment) in the seasons, the husband looks at and hears her, so the man with the fourteen vidyas sees the secret of the Veda's sense (dharma and Brahman); Vol 1 'on account of the season/night' vs new 'times of union', same sense.

Same: Yaska (Nirukta 1.20) cites 'uta tvam sakhye sthirapitam ahur nainam hinvanty api vajinesu, adhenva carati mayayaisa vacam susruvan aphalam apuspam'; the knower drinks the nectar of the sense, friendship of the Veda (sacividam sakhayam) or in heaven; vajinah = lords of speech/bold in assemblies who cannot oppose him; the mere reciter hears speech without flower (dharma, earlier part) and fruit (Brahman knowledge, later part).

Same: flower yields fruit as dharma-knowledge yields desire for Brahma-knowledge (tam etam vedanuvacanena brahmana vividisanti ...), Brahma-knowledge gives satisfaction ('yat purnanandaikabodhas tad brahmaham asmiti krtakrtyo bhavati'), the mere reciter goes about with the illusion of a cow, 'dhenu' = one that pleases, like a magician's cow. Detail: new 'nasakena' = 'by fasting', Vol 1 'austerity free from mortification'; new cites Paramahamsa Upanisad 4, Vol 1 gives no reference.

Same: what is praised is enjoined, so knowing the sense is enjoined like study; the Naksatresti sentence 'yatha ha va agnir devanam annado evam ha va esa manusyanam bhavati ya etena havisa yajate ya u caitad evam veda' gives the same fruit for sacrificing and for knowing; so all Brahmanas contain injunctions of knowing.

Same: Jaimini 'vidya-prasamsa' (1-2-15) makes the fruits of knowing praise; answered that praise may use an existing fruit, as 'svargaya hi lokaya darsapurnamasav ijyete' (TS 2.2.5.4) in the expiation for a lapse; the teacher's two verses 'icchamy evarthavadatvam vacaso 'nyaparatvatah ... na tv abhutarthavadata'; performance not useless since fruit varies in quantity or quality (Jaimini 1-2-17 'phalasya karmanispatteh ...').
Same: illustrated by 'tarati brahmahatyam yo 'svamedhena yajate ya u cainam eva veda'.

Same: Chandogas (CU 1.1.10) 'tenobhau kuruto yas caitad eva veda yas ca na veda; nana tu vidya cavidya ca; yad eva vidyaya karoti sraddhayopanisada tad eva viryavattaram bhavati' and same principle for all knowledge. New says 'knowledge' here means meditation on the part [of the Saman] (Sanskrit 'angavabodhopastih'); Vol 1 says 'special reference to a knowledge of the Angas of the Veda'; both render the same word, new nearer the Sanskrit and the Udgitha context; no clash.

Same: 'why so much devotion to knowing?' - rather praise shown and nowhere blame; the unseen of knowledge goes with the soul as that of action does; Vajasaneyin 'tam vidyakarmani samanvarabhete purvaprajna ca' (SB 14.7.2.3).
